title: ValidationRule
description: A declarative integrity constraint, declared in the data store's schema or collection configuration and enforced by the storage engine itself, that restricts which records, field values, keys or cross-collection references a write may produce. Application-side validation that the engine never sees, and imperative checks coded in triggers or procedures, are not instances. Use EventHandler instead when the check is imperative logic fired by a change event, such as a BEFORE INSERT trigger that raises an exception, rather than a declared constraint. Use Index instead when the declaration is an index created mainly to speed up lookups; a UNIQUE or PRIMARY KEY constraint that the engine happens to back with an index is still a validationrule. Use Field instead when the only restriction is the field's declared dataType, nullable flag, default or generation rule, with no separately named or declared constraint. Use RetentionPolicy instead when the rule governs how long data is kept and expires, deletes, archives or downsamples it, rather than rejecting or flagging invalid writes.

ruleType.description: Type of validation or integrity rule. SQL-standard: PRIMARY_KEY, FOREIGN_KEY, UNIQUE, CHECK, NOT_NULL. Document store: SCHEMA_VALIDATION (JSON Schema validator), REQUIRED_FIELD. Key-value: KEY_FORMAT (key naming pattern), TTL_CONSTRAINT. Graph: UNIQUENESS_CONSTRAINT (unique node label+property), EXISTENCE_CONSTRAINT (required property), NODE_KEY (composite unique identifier). Vector: DIMENSION_CONSTRAINT (vector dimension enforcement). Search engine: MAPPING_STRICT (reject unmapped fields). CUSTOM: engine-specific rule not listed.

expression.description: Constraint expression or validation rule body. For CHECK constraints, the SQL expression. For SCHEMA_VALIDATION, a JSON Schema reference. For KEY_FORMAT, a key naming pattern.

targetFields.description: Field name(s) this rule applies to.

referencedCollection.description: For FOREIGN_KEY or cross-collection references, the target collection name.

referencedFields.description: For FOREIGN_KEY or cross-collection references, the target field name(s) in the referenced collection.

onDelete.description: Referential action on delete. CASCADE: delete dependent entries. SET_NULL: nullify the reference. SET_DEFAULT: reset to default value. RESTRICT: reject if referenced entries exist. NO_ACTION: deferred reject. Applicable to FOREIGN_KEY rules.

onUpdate.description: Referential action on update. Same values as onDelete, applied when the referenced field value is modified. Applicable to FOREIGN_KEY rules.

enforcement.description: How the rule is enforced. STRICT: reject violating operations (default for most SQL constraints). WARN: allow but emit a warning (supported by some document store validators). LOG: allow and log the violation for audit purposes.

x-dr-standard: ISO/IEC 9075-2 (SQL/Foundation) §11.6 <table constraint definition>, with §11.7 unique, §11.8 referential and §11.9 check constraint definitions
x-dr-evidence: Migration or DDL statements containing constraint clauses, such as ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT, PRIMARY KEY (...), FOREIGN KEY ... REFERENCES ... ON DELETE CASCADE, or CHECK (...).

Engine-level validator or constraint commands, such as MongoDB createCollection/collMod with validator: {$jsonSchema: ...} and validationAction, or Neo4j CREATE CONSTRAINT ... REQUIRE n.email IS UNIQUE / IS NOT NULL.

ORM or schema-config declarations that emit engine constraints, such as SQLAlchemy CheckConstraint/UniqueConstraint/ForeignKey, Django Meta.constraints, or an Elasticsearch mapping with "dynamic": "strict".
